title: Agent Protocols: MCP vs ACP vs A2A
summary: MCP, Zed's Agent Client Protocol (ACP), and A2A solve different interoperability boundaries: tools/data, editor-to-agent integration, and independent agent-to-agent collaboration respectively.
eli5: Think of three plugs for three boundaries: MCP helps an agent reach tools and context; Zed ACP helps an editor talk to a coding agent; A2A helps one independent agent collaborate with another.

sections.heading: The shortest useful comparison
rows: Client/model application ↔ tool, resource or server
Expose callable capabilities and context through a standard protocol
Let editing environments integrate agents without a custom adapter for every pair
Discover capabilities, exchange messages/artifacts and coordinate tasks across agent systems

sections.heading: MCP: capabilities and context
sections.body: Model Context Protocol standardizes how an AI application interacts with MCP servers that expose tools and related capabilities. The July 28, 2026 MCP specification moved the core protocol to stateless request/response operation: requests are self-describing, discovery is optional, routing information can travel in headers, and extensions cover capabilities that do not belong in the minimal core.

sections.heading: Zed ACP: the editor-agent boundary
sections.body: The Agent Client Protocol created by Zed is an open protocol for connecting agents to editing environments. Its interoperability target is not primarily a generic tool server or a remote peer agent: it lets an editor/client provide a consistent interface to coding agents so capabilities such as context, editing and agent interaction do not require a bespoke integration for each editor-agent pair.

sections.heading: A2A: independent agent collaboration
sections.body: Agent2Agent (A2A) is designed for communication between independent, potentially opaque agent systems. Its specification covers capability discovery, interaction modalities, task collaboration and secure exchange without requiring one agent to know the other's internal memory or tools. The current official specification lists 1.0.0 as the latest released version.

sections.heading: ACP is an overloaded acronym
sections.body: Here ACP means Zed's Agent Client Protocol. Other projects have used the same letters for different agent-communication protocols. Always expand the acronym before comparing architectures; otherwise it is easy to compare different standards as if they were the same thing.

sections.heading: Do they compete?
rows: Often complementary: an agent can use MCP to access tools while using A2A to collaborate with another agent.
Different boundary: tool/context protocol versus client/editor-to-agent protocol.
Should every API become a protocol server?
No. Add a protocol facade only when interoperability, model-oriented semantics, discovery or policy boundaries justify the extra layer.
Does a protocol make an agent reliable?
No. Protocols standardize interfaces; correctness still depends on permissions, tool semantics, context, validation, retries and application design.

sections.heading: Architecture scenario
sections.question: A coding assistant runs inside an IDE, needs repository tools, and sometimes delegates a specialized task to a remote agent. Which protocol belongs where?
sections.diagnosis: There are three distinct boundaries rather than one universal protocol boundary.
sections.resolution: Use an editor-agent protocol such as Zed ACP at the IDE boundary when applicable, MCP where standardized tool/context access is useful, and A2A when the remote system is an independent peer agent exposing agent-level capabilities. Do not add all three unless those boundaries actually exist.

sections.heading: Check yourself
sections.question: Why is 'MCP vs A2A' often the wrong first question?
sections.answer: Because they commonly address different layers. MCP is centered on exposing tools/context/capabilities to AI applications; A2A is centered on collaboration between independent agents. A system may use both.
